title: RESPV6 Respiratory Virus Quantification on Bio-Rad QX600 Digital Droplet PCR System
author: Melissa Pitton
materials: Bio-Rad QX600 Digital Droplet PCR System

This protocol can be used on wastewater extracts, obtained by extracting total nucleic acids from raw wastewater samples, where MHV is spiked into part of the samples pre-extraction and PCR inhibitors are removed post-extraction. This protocol specifically describes the use of the RESPV6 assay on the Bio-Rad QX600 Digital Droplet PCR System, targeting SARS-CoV-2 N1 and N2 genes, IAV M-gene, IBV M-gene, RSV N-gene and MHV.
Switch on the UV light for 20 minutes.
Work in the PCR Template box.
Verify that all required materials have been correctly loaded into the AutoDG system.
Use the PTC Tempo Thermal Cycler (Bio-Rad).
Work in the PCR Mastermix box.
Put all the Mastermix reagents back in the -20°C freezer.

steps.title: Prepare Workspace and Reagents
steps.instruction: Clean and sterilize the PCR mastermix and template boxes and thaw necessary reagents.

substeps.instruction: Clean PCR mastermix and template boxes with RNAse away and dry with tissues.
Thaw nuclease-free water aliquot, primer and probe mixes, supermix, reverse transcriptase, and DTT from -20°C freezer at room temperature.
Vortex primer and probe mixes, supermix, reverse transcriptase, and DTT for 30 sec and spin down.

steps.title: Prepare Mastermix
steps.instruction: Create the PCR Mastermix in a sterile environment.

substeps.instruction: Label a 1.5 or 2.0 mL centrifuge tube as 'Mastermix' and place it in the PCR Mastermix box.
Prepare Mastermix according to manufacturer's instructions (volumes per sample as per Table 1) by pipetting reagents into the tube.
Vortex and spin down the Mastermix, then place it in the PCR Template box.
Empty the waste bin, clean the PCR Mastermix box with RNAse Away, and switch on UV light for 20 minutes.

steps.title: Sterilize Template Box and Equipment
steps.instruction: Prepare the PCR Template box and pipettes for sample loading.

substeps.instruction: Place two 96-well plates in the PCR Template box (one for samples, one for droplet generation).
Place the multistep pipet, multichannel pipet, and pipet tips in the PCR Template box.
Switch on the UV light for 20 minutes.

steps.title: Dispense Mastermix and Samples
steps.instruction: Load the 96-well plate with Mastermix, samples, and controls.

substeps.instruction: Dispense 16.8 µL Mastermix into each well using a multistep pipette (use a centrifuge tube PCR cooler if pipetting more than 1/4 of the plate).
Thaw RESPV6 positive control from -20°C at room temperature, then vortex and spin down.
Thaw wastewater extracts (from fridge or -80°C freezer), vortex and spin down (keep extracts and positive control on ice during pipetting).
Transfer 5.6 µL of wastewater extract into the correct wells, changing tips for each sample.
Pipette 5.6 µL of RESPV6 positive control into designated wells.
Pipette 5.6 µL of nuclease-free water into no-template control wells; discard aliquot after use.
Return wastewater extracts to 4°C fridge.
If fewer than 8 wells are used in a column, add 22.4 µL of 1x Buffer Control to the remaining wells.

steps.title: Seal and Prepare Plate
steps.instruction: Seal the sample plate and ensure it is free of bubbles.

substeps.instruction: Place an aluminium foil sheet on top of the plate, ensuring the red line is visible on the upper side.
Remove the plate from the PCR Template box.
Empty the waste bin, clean the PCR Template box with RNAse Away, and switch on UV light for 20 minutes.
Warm up the plate sealer to 180°C.
Place the plate on the metal block and seal (180°C for 5 s), ensuring the red line is on the upper side.
Remove the metal block from the sealer.
Vortex and centrifuge the sealed plate (1 min at 1,000 RCF, e.g., using CVP-2 'Spin Mix Spin' program).
Visually check for bubbles; repeat centrifugation if many small bubbles are present.

steps.title: Configure AutoDG System
steps.instruction: Set up the Automated Droplet Generation (AutoDG) system.

substeps.instruction: Ensure 'Automated Droplet Generation Oil for Probes' is installed.
Place an empty 96-well 'Droplet Plate' in the cooling block (previously UV sterilized).
Retrieve a cooling block from -20°C (must have been frozen for at least 2 h; color should be dark purple, not pink) and place it in the AutoDG 'Droplet plate' position.
Place the sealed sample plate in the 'Sample plate' position (well A1 at top-left).
Load AutoDG pipet boxes (remove wrapping and lid); use two columns of tips for every one column of samples.
Install cartridges and white rack (green side on the right-hand side).
Return the spare cooling block to the -20°C freezer upside-down.

steps.title: Run Droplet Generation
steps.instruction: Execute the droplet generation process and handle plates.

substeps.instruction: Click 'Configure Sample Plate' and select the filled columns.
Click 'Start Run' and keep the lid closed (~45 min for one full plate).
While running, store wastewater extracts in the -80°C freezer.
Once complete, remove both plates within 30 minutes.
Discard the 'Sample Plate' and reseal the 'Droplet Plate' using the sealer and aluminium foil (following the sealing/vortexing workflow).
Remove empty pipet tip boxes, trash cartridges and tips, and decontaminate the 'Tip Waste Bin' with RNAse Away and 20 min UV light.

steps.title: Quantification on QX600 Reader
steps.instruction: Load the droplet plate into the QX600 and run the quantification program.

substeps.instruction: Turn on the QX600 reader and connected computer; verify the first 3 indicator lights are green.
Open the reader lid and insert the 'Droplet Plate' using the metallic plate holder (well A1 top left), securing with black tabs.
Verify oil levels (green light = OK, blinking green = low, blinking orange = too low).
Open 'QX Manager Standard Edition' software.
Click 'Add Plate' and 'Configure Plate' to insert plate information.
Upload a Plate Template using a name filler and exclude unnecessary wells via 'Well Selection'.
Select program RESPV6 (ramp rate 2°C/second, lid temperature 105°C, well volume 40 µL).
Click 'Start Run' to begin reading.

steps.title: Export Data
steps.instruction: Export the final results from the software.

substeps.instruction: Click on 'Data Table'.
Click the 'hamburger' icon in the top right corner and select 'Export to CSV'.
Save the file to the desired path.
